key_insight: EgoGeneralist connects first-person video and metric 3D human motion in one modeling framework. It adapts pretrained video generators so actions can both guide video creation and be recovered from video.
problem_solved: Pretrained video models have strong visual knowledge but do not natively represent human actions in metric 3D space, limiting unified motion control, pose estimation, and action-video generation.
method: Adapt pretrained video generators to support action-conditioned egocentric video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation.
Use a role-adaptive action renderer to represent metric motion in a video-native form.
Enable multidirectional action-video learning, treating motion as both a spatial control signal and a recoverable generation target.
impact: The framework offers a unified approach to tasks often handled by separate models, making pretrained video generators more useful for motion-aware AI. The supplied abstract does not report quantitative results.
visual_elements: A three-branch task diagram: action → first-person video, video → 3D pose, and joint action + video generation.
A pipeline showing metric 3D motion → role-adaptive action renderer → video-native representation → pretrained video generator.
Paired first-person video frames and 3D skeletons illustrating the connection between appearance and motion.
A central model icon linked to three task icons to emphasize the unified framework.
paper_title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
paper_authors: Yanlin Jin, Bowen Yang, Cheng Zhang, Yifan Yang, Zhe Li
